الرَّخاءُ and الرُّخاءُ are lexical vocalic variants, not separate additional rows.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%84%D8%AD%D9%88. The Academy labels the weak-final lexicographic entry لحو and attests لَحَا, لَحَى, أَلْحَى, الْتَحَى, اللِّحاء, اللَّحْي, اللِّحية and المِلْحاة.
Academy uses the conventional weak-root label لحو; the project’s aligned Qur’anic data uses لحي. This is a documented normalization difference, not a change of lexical family.
لِحْيَةٌ was not added: it is the same lexical noun already present inside the current بِـ...ـي surface, so adding it would be shell/possessive removal rather than a new Ṣarf member.
The Academy’s root label لحو is recorded as an alternate weak-root normalization; project/Qur’anic provider canonical root لحي is retained and every candidate is mapped to that canonical family.

The approved evidence securely establishes the intestinal noun and its singular/plural relationship, but not four additional learner-useful same-root derivations. Treating the Academy label ماعي and the project/Qur’anic root معي as silently identical would be unsafe, so this is confirmed-limited with the normalization difference recorded.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%85%D8%A7%D8%B9%D9%8A. The Academy defines المَعَى/المِعَى as part of the intestines, with plural أَمْعاء, and labels the entry root ماعي.

Academy labels this lexical entry ماعي; project/Qur’anic provider data uses معي. The project root key is retained for aligned occurrence data, while the root meaning is corrected to the intestinal lexical branch.
مِعًى is a vocalic variant of the same lexical noun, not a second independent row.
The old project root-picture gloss meaning ‘being with someone’ is unrelated to this occurrence and was corrected to ‘intestine · intestinal tract’.
Generated verbs or participles were rejected because the approved evidence does not establish them for this lexical branch.
مِعًى: The Academy records it as a pronunciation variant of المَعَى, not an independent morphological family member.

The current Qur’anic form plus four independently attested, morphologically useful same-root forms are established. Weak-final alternation is explained honestly; no shell, case, pronoun or bare-radical padding is used.
